newsitem.title: CHINA: Shenzhen stock exchange urged to remake sub-index.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen stock exchange urged to remake sub-index.

text.p: China's top financial newspaper, China Securities, on Wednesday called on the Shenzhen stock exchange to re-configure its main stock sub-index, saying it was becoming unrepresentative as the market expanded.
The newspaper said in a front page article that the exchange's main sub-index was composed of only 40 stocks while the exchange now lists more than 300 companies.
The sub-index was launched in January 1995, and the list of constituent companies has not been revised since.
"Some of the 40 companies that make up the index have turned in poor results and are not representative of trends in their respective business areas," the newspaper said.
"The weighting of some stocks in the index is too high," it added.
It specifically referred to Shenzhen Development Bank, which accounts for 32.76 percent of the sub-index.
The bank's president was removed from office last month and the bank's shares were suspended for several days in punishment for illegal trading by the bank in its own shares.
The newspaper said some investors had sought to control the market by speculating in the bank's shares.
